info.help:
usage: wgsextract info [-h] [--detailed] [--format {tsv,parquet}] [--csv] <command> ...

positional arguments:
  <command>
    calculate-coverage  Generate a full breadth-of-coverage report. Uses samtools coverage to
                        calculate exactly how much of each chromosome was sequenced.
    coverage-sample     Quickly estimate per-chromosome breadth of coverage by sampling ~1,000
                        evenly spaced, length-weighted 1 kb windows. An estimate; use calculate-
                        coverage for exact numbers.
    chip                Identify the vendor, chip and revision of a consumer microarray raw-data
                        file (23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage, FTDNA, ...) from its header and
                        marker set, with a confidence score and the matching --formats template.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --detailed            Perform full index and body sample analysis (detailed mode)
  --format {tsv,parquet}
                        Also save the per-chromosome table and the QC stats as <input>_chromosomes
                        and <input>_qc .tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow); implies --detailed
  --csv                 Output the table as CSV instead of formatted text

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

examples:
  wgsextract info --input sample.cram
  wgsextract info --input sample.cram --detailed
  wgsextract info --input sample.cram --format parquet

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  Prints a summary and caches it as <input file name>.wgse_info.json; with
  --format also <input file name>_chromosomes and _qc (QC stats) as .tsv or
  .parquet.

needs:
  samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools; seconds on a 30x
  genome.

microarray.help:
usage: wgsextract microarray [-h] [--formats FORMATS] [--format {tsv,parquet}] [--sample SAMPLE]
                             [-r REGION] [--help-all]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --formats FORMATS     Comma-separated list of formats to generate (default: all).
                        Available formats:
                          Combined kit only (always written):
                            all (every chip's markers in one 23andMe-style file, e.g. for GEDmatch;
                            writes no vendor files: list the vendor formats to get them)
                          23andMe:
                            23andme_v2 (also v1: same markers), 23andme_v3, 23andme_v4, 23andme_v5,
                            23andme_v5_2025 (v5 chip as exported in 2025), 23andme_v3+v5, 23andme_api
                          AncestryDNA:
                            ancestry_v1, ancestry_v2, ancestry_v2_2021 (2021 V2.0 layout),
                            ancestry_v2_2024 (V2.0 chip as exported in 2024-25)
                          Family Tree DNA:
                            ftdna_v1 (Affymetrix, NCBI36 positions), ftdna_v2, ftdna_v3
                          Living DNA:
                            ldna_v1, ldna_v2
                          MyHeritage:
                            myheritage_v1, myheritage_v2,
                            myheritage_gsa_2025 (609,346 markers), myheritage_gsa_2025_609424
                          Nucleus:
                            nucleus (array export, 2025)
                          AADR v66.p1 (GRCh37 outputs, PLINK .bed/.bim/.fam AND EIGENSTRAT .geno/.snp/.ind):
                            aadr_1240k, aadr_ho, aadr_1240k+ho (HO is a subset of 1240K in this release)
                            aadr_2m (opt-in; first run 'ref aadr --install'; v66.p1 genetic distances
                              differ from legacy 1240K/HO at 1,200,251 sites; maps are never mixed)
  --format {tsv,parquet}
                        Also save the genotypes as <input>_genotypes.tsv or .parquet (needs pyarrow): rsID, chrom, pos (in the input's build) and genotype
  --sample SAMPLE       Sample to use from a multi-sample VCF (e.g. a joint-called nf-core/sarek VCF); required when the VCF has more than one
  -r, --region REGION   Chromosomal region (e.g. chrM, chrY:10000-20000)
  --help-all            Show this help with the advanced options too, and exit.

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json,
  --quiet, --debug, --config and the other global options are accepted before
  or after the command; 'wgsextract --help' lists them all.

15 advanced options not shown; 'wgsextract microarray --help-all' lists them.

examples:
  wgsextract microarray --input sample.cram --formats 23andme_v5
  wgsextract microarray --input sample.cram --formats 23andme_v5,ancestry_v2

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  <input stem>_<format>.txt (or the vendor's extension) per format, such as
  sample_23andMe_V5.txt, and <input stem>_CombinedKit.txt; with --format also
  <input stem>_genotypes.tsv or .parquet.

needs:
  bcftools, bgzip, samtools, tabix; depending on options and inputs, also:
  curl; minutes on a 30x genome.

report.help:
usage: wgsextract report [-h] [--workspace DIR] [--results DIR] [--format {tsv,parquet}]

Summarise a sample's results (overview, QC, lineage, pharmacogenomics, ClinVar pathogenic calls in
ACMG SF genes, microarray files) as a local HTML, Markdown and JSON report with confidence-
labelled findings. Reads earlier runs' result manifests; runs no analysis and makes no network
calls. Technical results, not diagnosis.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --workspace DIR       Sample folder whose results are reported (default: the --genome folder,
                        else the --input's folder).
  --results DIR         Also read result manifests from this folder (repeatable); only runs on
                        this sample's files are used. The --outdir is always read.
  --format {tsv,parquet}
                        Format of the findings table, <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv or
                        .parquet (needs pyarrow) (default: tsv)

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

examples:
  wgsextract report --genome HG002
  wgsextract report --input sample.cram
  wgsextract report --workspace HG002 --results ~/wgs-out/HG002 --format parquet

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  <sample>_personal_report.html, .md and .json and
  <sample>_personal_report_findings.tsv (or .parquet with --format parquet) in
  the sample folder (or --outdir); evidence links are relative to the sample
  folder.

needs:
  no external tools; seconds from existing results.
